subject: ACME POC kickoff recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dan Jacobs <dan.jacobs@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: ACME POC kickoff recap & next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Dan — good conversation. Below is a short recap from our discovery and a proposed scope/timeline for the pilot so we can get the engineering work scoped and scheduled. Please confirm or flag anything that’s off.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Latency variability on current LLM endpoints impacting product UX (spikes to >500ms p95).
- Per-token cost is high during peak batch jobs — want clearer unit economics.
- Need stable, auditable inference for compliance (audit logs + access controls).
- Business goal: roll a production reranking/generation feature into the customer funnel with 99th pct availability and predictable cost.

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- 2-week focused pilot (hosted Redwood API + optional dedicated capacity if needed).
- Workload: reranking + light generation on a 50-prompt seed set you provide.
- Success metrics: latency p95 < 200ms; end-to-end throughput to meet 50 reqs/s; quality: precision@5 >= 0.62 on your labelled eval set; cost target: reduce tokens/unit cost by >=20% vs current baseline.
- Deliverables: evaluation report, prompts/eval sheet, tuning suggestions (batching/quantization), and a runbook for production rollout.

Owners & roles
- Redwood AE / project owner: Marissa Cole (me) — commercial and SOW coordination.
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao — access/setup, model selection, evaluation harness, and prompt tuning.
- ACME technical lead: Dan Jacobs — provide access to eval labels, sample traffic patterns, and 50-prompt seed set.
- ACME product: Priya Shah — acceptance criteria and business sign-off.

Timeline (proposed)
- Wed 2026-06-23: Kickoff call + environment access (team check-in, confirm prompt set).
- 2026-06-24 to 2026-07-03: POC execution (data ingest, eval runs, tuning).
- 2026-07-06: Review results and next steps / decision.

Access & setup steps we need from ACME
1) Share the 50-prompt seed set and a small labelled eval file (CSV) in the shared Drive folder.
2) Provide a service account or API credentials for test traffic (if you want us to run through your VPC/Dedicated environment, we’ll need network contacts — else we can run on hosted).
3) Confirm any compliance evidence you require (we attached our SOC 2 summary and access setup doc).

Attachments: acme_poc_scope_v1.pdf (scope + SOW draft), redwood-access-setup.md (setup checklist), acme-poc-prompt-set.csv (template).

Next steps / asks
- Dan / Priya: confirm kickoff on 2026-06-23 or propose an alternate date.
- Share the prompt set and eval labels by EOD 2026-06-22 so Aditya can start prepping the harness.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the clear summary, Marissa — this aligns with our notes. A few clarifications: 

- Timeline: can we move kickoff to Mon 2026-06-22 instead of the 23rd? Our engineering lead is out on the 23rd.
- Data access: we prefer to run the POC on Redwood hosted initially, but we will need logs/audit info exported to our S3 for compliance. Can you confirm Redwood can push logs to our S3 bucket or provide a daily export?
- Eval metrics: precision@5 target looks reasonable, but can we add a secondary qualitative check (10 manual samples reviewed by Priya) to complement the metrics?

I’ll attach the initial prompt set and a small labelled eval sample in a follow-up email by EOD. Also looping Priya so she sees the acceptance criteria.

—Dan

- 10:15–11:00: SE deep-dive: access, traffic profile, prompt set, evaluation harness (Aditya).
